nodes.info: Reptiles are an important clade of land animal, sister to modern mammals. Prior to the K-Pg Boundary Event 65 million years ago, the clade had significantly more diversity.
nodes.name: Reptiles

nodes.info: This is the least diverse of the two basal clades of reptile, and was discovered through molecular evidence from genome sequencing, challenging the traditional belief that turtles were more closely-related to snakes than to birds. Subsequent anatomical studies have identified the presence of a sagittal crest on the supraoccipital bone and a lack of the entepicondylar foramen on the humerus as diagnostic of this clade.
nodes.name: Archelosauria

nodes.info: The clade which contains modern birds and crocodilians - along with all extinct dinosaurs and pterosaurs. Diagnostic of this clade are the fenestrae behind the eyes, as well as the unique four-chambered heart design.
nodes.name: Archosauria

nodes.info: A clade of large, predatory, semi-aquatic reptiles. These large species are covered in bony armor-plates and have long, flat tails and webbed feet.
nodes.name: Crocodilians

nodes.info: A clade distinct for its broad snout, hidden lower teeth, and freshwater environment.
nodes.name: Alligatoridae

nodes.info: Distinct for their bony septum and cold-temperature tolerance.
nodes.name: Alligators

nodes.info: A clade unique for the bony ridge between the eyes and needle-like nose.
nodes.name: Caimans

nodes.info: The clade of crocodilian most amenable to salt water thanks to specialized exchange glands as well as an interlocking and exposed fourth-tooth.
nodes.name: Crocodiles

nodes.info: The clade containing the modern birds, and also containing the most famous extinct animals in the world thanks to books, television, and movies. Unique features of this clade include an open hip socket and fused vertebrae in the lower back to accommodate an upright posture.
nodes.name: Dinosaurs

nodes.info: The only living clade of flying reptiles, birds possess a characteristic wing with an elongated upper arm - even in flightless species. They also lack the tails of other theropods.
nodes.name: Birds

nodes.info: Turtles are a clade of reptile distinguished by a bony composite shell over their bodies. As with all reptiles, turtles descend from swimming, underwater vertebrates - but in the case of modern surviving turtles, their ancestors actually went back into the water, and the modern land-dwelling turtles emerged again.
nodes.name: Turtles

nodes.info: The most diverse clade of reptiles, containing the tuatara, and all lizards.
nodes.name: Lepidosaurs

nodes.info: The most diverse clade of lepidosaur, featuring a common "lizard-like" body plan and its derivatives. Unique for their paired hemipenes in male reproduction, as well as skull kinesis and skin shedding.
nodes.name: Lizards (Squamata)

nodes.info: Snakes are a legless clade of lizard. They possess a highly mobile, kinetic skull; they lack movable eyelids; and, they accommodate their paired organs sequentially in their long, slender bodies.
nodes.name: Snakes

nodes.info: The sole surviving species of the ancient clade Rhynchocephalia, unique for their possession of the ancestral form of the diapsid skull, keeping intact both the upper and lower temporal bars.
nodes.name: Tuatara
